subject: 2023 Park Permit and Fee Updates
overview: The Medford Park Commission addressed public concerns over court congestion and updated the 2023 permit application process. The board approved fee increases for Wright’s Pond and Tufts Pool while tabling a decision on expanding pickleball courts.

items.title: Public Comment on Court Usage
items.summary: Residents expressed concerns regarding limited tennis court availability at Playstead Park and the impact of pickleball at Dugger Park.

items.title: Tennis and Pickleball Scheduling
items.summary: The board discussed court allocation strategies for youth and adult programs across city parks and decided to revisit scheduling policies in March.

items.title: 2023 Field Permit Application
items.summary: Approved updates to the permit application, including a new procedure for posting field closure alerts on the recreation website.

items.title: Rental Fee Structure
items.summary: Updated field and court rental fees to include hourly rates and established a two-hour minimum for private rentals.

items.title: Interdepartmental Permit Coordination
items.summary: Decided to require applicants to obtain sign-offs from the Health and Police departments for special events prior to the final issuance of a park permit.

items.title: Memorials and Dedications
items.summary: Approved a standardized request form to streamline the approval process for plaques, benches, and other park memorials on a case-by-case basis.

items.title: Wright’s Pond and Tufts Pool Fees
items.summary: Approved a 10% fee increase for pond and pool passes and introduced a caregiver pass for residents requiring a driver to access the facilities.

items.title: Dugger Park Pickleball Expansion
items.summary: Tabled a decision on lining a sixth pickleball court at Dugger Park until the results of a community survey are presented in February.

items.title: Maintenance and Routine Items
items.summary: Addressed concerns regarding soccer net security at Harris Park and discussed ongoing maintenance delays at the state-managed pandemic memorial.
